title: Tata's Taj and Adani's airports team up for 8 hotels with over 2,000 rooms
subtitle: Adani will build the hotels at the airports it runs in Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati, and IHCL will run them as Taj, Vivanta, Gateway and Ginger.
content_html:
Picture this. Your flight lands in Guwahati late at night. Instead of hunting for a taxi into the city, you walk a few steps and check into a Taj. That is the plan behind a deal signed on Thursday, 29 October 2026.

On that day, Tata group's Indian Hotels Company (IHCL) and Adani Airport Holdings (AAHL) announced an agreement for eight hotels with over 2,000 rooms. The hotels will sit at airports run by Adani in Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati. So the Tata group and the Adani group are now working together on the same project.

What exactly did they sign?

IHCL owns several hotel brands, each for a different budget. Think of them like seats at a cricket stadium, from the fancy box to the regular stands. Mint describes Taj as premium luxury and Vivanta as upscale, and calls Ginger "lean luxe", which means simple rooms that still feel nice. Together with Gateway, the brands cover luxury, upscale and midscale travellers.

The eight hotels break down like this:

  • Mumbai: one Taj, now being built at Terminal 2 of the airport.
  • Ahmedabad: one Taj and one Vivanta, both in advanced stages of construction.
  • Lucknow: one Vivanta and one Ginger.
  • Guwahati: one Taj, one Gateway and one Ginger.

That makes three Taj hotels, two Vivanta, one Gateway and two Ginger. Business Standard reported, citing people aware of the details, that most of these hotels should open in three to four years.

Who builds and who runs?

This is the clever part. Adani's company will develop the hotels. IHCL will run them under its own brand names. In business language, this is called an operating agreement.

Think of a samosa stall. One person owns the land and builds the stall. A famous samosa brand then runs it. The brand brings its name, its recipe and its way of serving customers. The owner gets a shop that people trust from day one. The brand grows without spending money on new buildings.

IHCL already does this a lot. In December 2025, it signed a 200 room Ginger hotel at Terminal 2 of Mumbai airport. In that deal, a Mumbai company called Hazoor Multiprojects is the owner, and IHCL is the one running the hotel.

Why build hotels right next to an airport?

Lots of people need a bed close to the runway. Some have a late flight. Some have a very early one. Some fly in for a single meeting and fly back the next day. Others get stuck when a flight is delayed.

Mint points out that hotels linked to airports can serve travellers changing flights, people on work trips, tourists and visitors coming for meetings and events. These hotels will also have places to eat, meeting rooms, spaces for events, wellness and fun, as per the same Business Standard report.

Jeet Adani, director of AAHL, put the bigger idea like this: "Across the world, leading airports are evolving into integrated destinations that serve as catalysts for commerce, tourism, and urban growth."

The bigger plan: airport cities

The hotels are one piece of a much larger puzzle. AAHL has set up a company called Adani Airport City Limited. Its job is to develop a land bank of over 655 acres across six airports. A land bank is land a company holds now so it can build on it later, like a plot your family keeps for a future house. Nearly 440 acres of this land is in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai.

In the first phase, Adani Airport City plans to invest over Rs 20,000 crore to build about 22 million square feet across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Jaipur and Guwahati, according to The Economic Times. The idea is to mix hotels, offices, shops and places to have fun around each airport.

This is not Adani's first hotel deal this year

In May 2026, the global hotel company IHG signed a deal with Adani Airport Holdings for five hotels with close to 1,500 rooms. Those are planned in Jaipur, Navi Mumbai, Mangaluru and Thiruvananthapuram. IHG calls AAHL India's largest private airport operator.

So Adani is doing what a cricket captain does with a strong team: picking different players for different roles. One hotel group here, another there, all on its airport land.

What does IHCL get out of this?

IHCL is an old name. Its first hotel, the Taj Mahal Palace in Mumbai, opened in 1903. Today it is India's largest hospitality player by market value, which means the total price of all its shares is the highest among Indian hotel companies.

With the eight new hotels, IHCL will have 25 hotels across its brands at key airports in India, said its MD and CEO Puneet Chhatwal. He called the deal a partnership between "two leading Indian companies with a shared vision to build India's travel and tourism sector".

Here is the simple idea. More flyers means more people who need a room near an airport, and a hotel right at the terminal is the closest room of all.

What changes for you?

For travellers, the choice gets wider. Someone on a tight budget can look at Ginger. A family on a special trip can look at Taj. Both will sit close to the flight.

For work, new hotels need people. A hotel needs front desk staff, cooks, cleaners and managers to run every day. The companies have not shared how many people they will hire, so no number can be given yet. But eight hotels in four cities, including Lucknow and Guwahati, could mean fresh roles in hospitality outside the usual big metros.

For cities, these hotels are part of a plan to turn airports into busy business areas, not just places you rush through.
